investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T10:58–11:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free capacity. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the production-api node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a contract misconfiguration.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' for the remote-agent-create pod stuck unscheduled for 134s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141297, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-08T11:00:38.624Z — the check timed out waiting for pod scheduling, not for agent readiness.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the runner never advancing past pod scheduling (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent is called but cannot complete).
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the probe returned before any VM was assigned.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 143s, empty evidenceKeys — same root cause.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 146s, empty evidenceKeys — same root cause.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled, the agent never reaches a ready state and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unschedulable.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads consuming that resource, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. A recent change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the node pool for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads may not have auto-scaled in time, or the maximum node count for that pool has been reached, preventing new nodes from joining to absorb demand.

Lower confidence — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a previous eval run may be holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot without releasing it, preventing new scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to prevent this, but a cleanup failure could cause slot leakage.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the two eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would be disproved and the cause would shift to a pod spec or API error.

If the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity selector did not match any node at all (i.e., 0 nodes had the required label), the failure would be a misconfiguration of node labels or the pod template rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run at a time of known low cluster load succeeded and produced all four required evidence keys, the failure would be transient capacity pressure rather than a structural exhaustion or misconfiguration.

If the cluster autoscaler logs showed a successful scale-out event that added a kata.peerpods.io/vm node between 10:58Z and 11:05Z but the pods still failed, the cause would be a pod spec or scheduler policy issue rather than capacity.

If only one of the three sibling checks failed (rather than all three with the same message), a shared infrastructure cause would be less likely and a check-specific configuration error would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for allocatable vs. used kata.peerpods.io/vm resources across all nodes and fails with a warning before capacity reaches zero, providing earlier signal than a pod scheduling timeout.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30 minutes) that are not in a terminal state, alerting before they exhaust node capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least one node in the cluster satisfies the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector requirements and carries non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, catching topology misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.

Refine the remote-agent-create check to distinguish between a scheduling failure (Unschedulable) and a post-scheduling failure (VM provisioning error, agent startup error) by capturing the pod phase and scheduler event in the evidence object, enabling more precise diagnosis in future failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-08T11:00–11:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for every remote-agents eval pod submitted during this run window. The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource — required for peer-pod / confidential-VM-backed remote agents — was fully consumed across the two eligible nodes, and preemption was not possible (no lower-priority victims found). As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) timed out waiting for the pod to become Running, the probe exited with the scheduling error message, and zero evidence keys were written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: only 2 of 6 cluster nodes carry this resource, and both were fully allocated when the eval pods were submitted. No preemption victims were available, so all three eval pods remained Unschedulable until the probe timeout.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata/peer-pod nodes satisfy. If the node pool was recently scaled down or nodes were cordoned/drained, the effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if the vm resource quota appeared non-zero.

TERTIARY — concurrent workload contention: other production workloads or a burst of user-initiated remote agents may have consumed the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both eligible nodes immediately before the eval run, leaving no capacity for the eval pods.

SPECULATIVE — eval run timing collision: all three sibling checks ran within the same ~5-minute window (11:00–11:05Z) and each attempted to create a separate remote agent pod, potentially competing with each other for the same exhausted resource pool.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T10:58–11:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free capacity. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the production-api node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a contract misconfiguration.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' for the remote-agent-create pod stuck unscheduled for 134s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141297, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-08T11:00:38.624Z — the check timed out waiting for pod scheduling, not for agent readiness.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the runner never advancing past pod scheduling (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent is called but cannot complete).
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the probe returned before any VM was assigned.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 143s, empty evidenceKeys — same root cause.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 146s, empty evidenceKeys — same root cause.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled, the agent never reaches a ready state and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unschedulable.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads consuming that resource, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. A recent change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the node pool for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads may not have auto-scaled in time, or the maximum node count for that pool has been reached, preventing new nodes from joining to absorb demand.

Lower confidence — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a previous eval run may be holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot without releasing it, preventing new scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to prevent this, but a cleanup failure could cause slot leakage.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the two eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would be disproved and the cause would shift to a pod spec or API error.

If the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity selector did not match any node at all (i.e., 0 nodes had the required label), the failure would be a misconfiguration of node labels or the pod template rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run at a time of known low cluster load succeeded and produced all four required evidence keys, the failure would be transient capacity pressure rather than a structural exhaustion or misconfiguration.

If the cluster autoscaler logs showed a successful scale-out event that added a kata.peerpods.io/vm node between 10:58Z and 11:05Z but the pods still failed, the cause would be a pod spec or scheduler policy issue rather than capacity.

If only one of the three sibling checks failed (rather than all three with the same message), a shared infrastructure cause would be less likely and a check-specific configuration error would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for allocatable vs. used kata.peerpods.io/vm resources across all nodes and fails with a warning before capacity reaches zero, providing earlier signal than a pod scheduling timeout.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30 minutes) that are not in a terminal state, alerting before they exhaust node capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least one node in the cluster satisfies the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector requirements and carries non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, catching topology misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.

Refine the remote-agent-create check to distinguish between a scheduling failure (Unschedulable) and a post-scheduling failure (VM provisioning error, agent startup error) by capturing the pod phase and scheduler event in the evidence object, enabling more precise diagnosis in future failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-08T11:00–11:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for every remote-agents eval pod submitted during this run window. The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource — required for peer-pod / confidential-VM-backed remote agents — was fully consumed across the two eligible nodes, and preemption was not possible (no lower-priority victims found). As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) timed out waiting for the pod to become Running, the probe exited with the scheduling error message, and zero evidence keys were written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: only 2 of 6 cluster nodes carry this resource, and both were fully allocated when the eval pods were submitted. No preemption victims were available, so all three eval pods remained Unschedulable until the probe timeout.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata/peer-pod nodes satisfy. If the node pool was recently scaled down or nodes were cordoned/drained, the effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if the vm resource quota appeared non-zero.

TERTIARY — concurrent workload contention: other production workloads or a burst of user-initiated remote agents may have consumed the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both eligible nodes immediately before the eval run, leaving no capacity for the eval pods.

SPECULATIVE — eval run timing collision: all three sibling checks ran within the same ~5-minute window (11:00–11:05Z) and each attempted to create a separate remote agent pod, potentially competing with each other for the same exhausted resource pool.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-07-08 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the agent creation step, so zero evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod during the eval window was rejected with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of user-traffic or broader service impact is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible cluster nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in all three check failure messages (evidence ids: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — Insufficient node pool size: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and match the pod's node affinity/selector. If those 2 nodes are sized with a low VM quota, even modest concurrent load will exhaust capacity.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming VM slots and not being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is responsible for teardown, but if a prior run was interrupted before cleanup, orphaned pods could be holding VM allocations.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration causing only 2 of 6 nodes to be eligible: if the affinity rules are overly restrictive, the effective scheduling pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes regardless of total cluster size.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node output showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create check passed in a subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held VM slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's specific pod spec or configuration rather than a shared cluster capacity problem.

If the node affinity/selector rules were found to match more than 2 nodes, the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would need re-examination and the diagnosis would shift toward a quota or admission webhook issue rather than affinity misconfiguration.

If orphaned pods from prior runs were found and deleted, and subsequent eval runs then passed, that would confirm the leaked-pod hypothesis as the primary cause rather than absolute cluster capacity limits.
